meta.location: Gideon, Zarahemla, Nephihah, and the land of Moroni
principles: A rebellion put down under law
A city taken by night without a death
A long war ending in two kinds of people

world_behind.title: The chapter resolves both wars at once
world_behind.text: The civil war with Pachus ends by verse 11 and the Lamanite war by verse 38. Alma 51:5 had opened the internal split with the king-men and Alma 43:4 the external war; this chapter closes conflicts that have run for eleven and nineteen chapters respectively.

world_behind.title: Pachus is named here for the first time
world_behind.text: Verse 6 identifies him as the king of the dissenters who drove the freemen out of Zarahemla. Alma 61:8 had reported the king without the name.

world_behind.title: The executions follow trials
world_behind.text: Verse 9 brings Pachus's followers and the jailed king-men to trial under the law, and puts them to death under it.

world_behind.title: Nephihah is retaken with cords and ladders
world_behind.text: Verses 20 through 23 have Moroni scout the wall by night and lower his whole force by cords and ladders into the empty western quarter. Alma 51:23 had reported the city lost because the Nephites were not sufficiently strong in it; Nephihah is the only city in the war taken back without the loss of one soul.

world_behind.title: Four thousand prisoners become farmers
world_behind.text: Verses 16, 17, and 29 have Lamanite prisoners covenant, join the people of Ammon, and take up tilling the ground. Alma 27:22 to 24 had settled that people in Jershon under Nephite protection, and Alma 53:5 had prisoners doing forced labor on fortifications. This is the same problem solved by absorption rather than by guards.

world_behind.title: Teancum dies on a private errand
world_behind.text: Verse 35 says only Teancum resolved on a stratagem that night, and gives his anger at Ammoron and Amalickiah as the reason. Alma 51:34 had him kill Amalickiah the same way and get out alive; this time the king wakes his servants first. The record reports the same operation twice with opposite outcomes.

world_behind.title: The record closes the war by describing people
world_behind.text: Verses 41 through 51 report that the same length of war hardened some and humbled others, and that prosperity returned without pride. Helaman 3:33 to 36 has the pride arriving anyway within twenty years, so this is the last stretch in the record where riches and humility are reported together.

words.text: Put to death by sentence of law. The record uses the word five times, twice in this chapter. Verses 9 and 10 attach it to trials, to the law, and to a specific offense.
Scaling equipment. Both of the record's uses are in this chapter, at verses 21 and 23, paired each time with strong cords. The word appears nowhere in the King James Bible.
Struck with sudden fear. The record uses it twice, at Alma 52:2 of the Lamanites finding Amalickiah dead, and here of Lamanites waking to find an army already inside the walls.
Treated at Alma 43:30, of Moroni dividing his army at Sidon. This is the war block's last use, and it belongs to one man acting alone at night.
Treated at Alma 51:34, where Teancum killed Amalickiah with one. The record gives him the same weapon and the same target eleven years later, with the opposite result.
Made tender or yielding. The record uses the word twelve times, first at 1 Nephi 2:16 of Nephi's heart. Verse 41 sets it against hardening, with the same cause producing both.

phrases.term: That he was not also a traitor to the freedom and cause of his country
phrases.text: Mormon reports the relief and repeats the accusation in the same clause. Alma 60:18 had made it, and the record retires it here.

phrases.term: He did raise the standard of liberty in whatsoever place he did enter
phrases.text: Moroni uses on his own countrymen what he first used against them in Alma 46. The march to Gideon doubles as a recruiting drive.

phrases.term: They were executed according to the law
phrases.text: Mormon states the procedure twice in one verse: trial according to the law, execution according to the law. The offense is named as refusing to defend the country and fighting against it.

phrases.term: Whosoever was found denying their freedom was speedily executed according to the law
phrases.text: The policy stated as a standing rule. Mormon calls it expedient for the safety of the country and gives no other justification.

phrases.term: They caused them to enter into a covenant that they would no more take up their weapons of war
phrases.text: Four thousand captured Lamanites swear the oath the Anti-Nephi-Lehies took in Alma 24. The record treats the covenant as sufficient security for release.

phrases.term: Strong cords and ladders, to be let down from the top of the wall
phrases.text: The equipment for taking Nephihah. Moroni had scouted the camp himself the night before and knew the western quarter was empty.

phrases.term: Without the loss of one soul
phrases.text: The city Moroni had grieved over in Alma 59:11 comes back at no Nephite cost. Mormon adds that many Lamanites were slain.

phrases.term: Desirous to join the people of Ammon and become a free people
phrases.text: Prisoners of war ask for the terms the Anti-Nephi-Lehies received. Verse 29 has them tilling ground and raising flocks, and relieving the Nephites of a burden.

phrases.term: Teancum in his anger did go forth into the camp of the Lamanites
phrases.text: The last stratagem of the war, and the only one Mormon attributes to anger. Verse 35 names the anger's cause before the raid begins.

phrases.term: Many had become hardened... and many were softened because of their afflictions
phrases.text: Mormon's summary of what the war did to the people. One length of war, one set of afflictions, and two results.

phrases.term: They were not lifted up in the pride of their eyes
phrases.text: The verse that measures the recovery. Riches, strength, and prosperity return, and Mormon says what did not come with them.

verses.label: v. 1–2
verses.title: Two opposite reactions to one letter
verses.text: The record reports both and does not reconcile them. Verse 1: "when Moroni had received this epistle his heart did take courage, and was filled with exceedingly great joy because of the faithfulness of Pahoran." Verse 2: "he did also mourn exceedingly because of the iniquity of those who had driven Pahoran from the judgment-seat." The same document produces joy about one man and grief about others, and the record gives each its own verse rather than folding them into a single mixed feeling.

verses.label: v. 9–10
verses.title: A civil war closed by trial, and the standard is stated
verses.text: The record does not report summary killings. It reports a legal process: "the men of Pachus received their trial, according to the law, and also those king-men who had been taken and cast into prison." Then the standard applied and its consequence: "whosoever was found denying their freedom was speedily executed according to the law." The verse before gives the rationale, "it became expedient that this law should be strictly observed for the safety of their country," so the record supplies the reasoning as well as the outcome.

verses.label: v. 39–41
verses.title: One cause, two opposite effects, stated together
verses.text: The record's summary of the long war refuses to generalise in one direction: "because of the exceedingly great length of the war between the Nephites and the Lamanites many had become hardened, because of the exceedingly great length of the war; and many were softened because of their afflictions." The same clause is repeated on both sides of the sentence, so the length of the war is given as the cause of hardening and of softening in the same breath. Verse 40 has already conceded the worst, "there had been murders, and contentions, and dissensions, and all manner of iniquity among the people of Nephi."

verses.label: v. 42–44
verses.title: A war ends with three men going back to work
verses.text: The record reports demobilisation as a set of resumptions rather than a ceremony. Moroni "yielded up the command of his armies into the hands of his son, whose name was Moronihah; and he retired to his own house that he might spend the remainder of his days in peace." Then "Pahoran did return to his judgment-seat," and "Helaman did take upon him again to preach unto the people the word of God." Three offices, three clauses, and the general's is the only one that ends rather than resumes.

verses.label: v. 48–51
verses.title: The pattern of the book, and the exception noted
verses.text: The volume's usual sequence runs prosperity, then pride, then decline. Here the record states the prosperity and then denies the second step outright: "notwithstanding their riches, or their strength, or their prosperity, they were not lifted up in the pride of their eyes; neither were they slow to remember the Lord their God." Verse 50 gives the reason as memory, "they did remember how great things the Lord had done for them," and verse 51 gives the practice, "they did pray unto the Lord their God continually." A reader who has watched the cycle turn a dozen times is shown it not turning.

chapter.title: Two wars end in one chapter
chapter.text: The civil war closes at verse 11 and the Lamanite war at verse 38. Mormon spends eleven verses on the first and twenty-seven on the second.

chapter.title: The executions are placed inside the law
chapter.text: Verses 9 and 10 name the trial, the statute, and the offense. Mormon reports the deaths as a legal outcome and calls the policy expedient for safety.

chapter.title: The covenant is treated as security
chapter.text: Four thousand armed enemies are released on an oath in verse 16. The record has been building that precedent since Alma 24 and Alma 44.

chapter.title: Prisoners become a labor force by their own request
chapter.text: Verses 27 through 29 have them asking for the terms and then farming. Mormon notes what this saved the Nephites.

chapter.title: Nephihah is taken by reconnaissance
chapter.text: Moroni scouts the wall himself in verse 20. The operation costs no Nephite life and turns on knowing where the enemy slept.

chapter.title: Teancum's death is reported without praise for the method
chapter.text: Verse 35 gives anger as the motive, verse 36 gives the failure, and verse 37 praises the man for valor and friendship to liberty.

chapter.title: The same war produced two kinds of people
chapter.text: Verse 41 puts hardening and humbling side by side with one cause. Mormon offers no ratio and no explanation.

chapter.title: The recovery is described by what did not happen
chapter.text: Verses 48 through 51 report riches and strength, then say the people were not lifted up and not slow to remember. Helaman 3 will report the other outcome a generation later.

applications.title: Drop the accusation once it is answered
applications.text: Moroni's response to the truth was joy, and the record never returns to the charge. When you were wrong about someone, close it fully.

applications.title: Recruit while you travel
applications.text: Moroni raised the standard of liberty in every place he entered on the march to Gideon and gathered whatever force he could as he went. A journey undertaken to deal with a problem is also time available for adding the people who will help you deal with it.

applications.title: Keep the procedure when the stakes are highest
applications.text: The men who had nearly cost the country the war still received trials. Emergency is the moment process is most likely to be skipped and most needed.

applications.title: Send the supplies the moment the way clears
applications.text: As soon as Zarahemla was secure, Moroni sent six thousand men with provisions to Helaman and six thousand more to Lehi and Teancum. When a blockage lifts, move first on what was waiting behind it, before fresh business fills the space.

applications.title: Scout before you commit
applications.text: Moroni went up the wall himself to see where the enemy slept, and the assault cost nothing. An hour of looking can replace a battle.

applications.title: Give people a way back in
applications.text: Four thousand prisoners asked to become a free people and were granted it, and the burden of guarding them disappeared. Terms that let an opponent join you can cost less than holding them.

applications.title: Do not go over the wall angry
applications.text: Teancum let himself down alone into the Lamanite camp because he was exceedingly wroth with Ammoron, killed him, and was killed. Anger will supply the courage a solo operation needs and none of the other things it needs.

applications.title: Ask which way the long stretch is working on you
applications.text: Mormon writes that the exceeding length of the war made many hardened and made many humble. Duration by itself settles nothing, so check periodically which of the two it has been doing to you.

questions.text: What accusation of mine is still standing after the facts came in?
What am I raising in every place I go?
Where have I let urgency talk me out of due process?
Whose word have I decided I can accept?
What am I about to commit to without having looked?
What has my anger sent me out to do alone?
The same year hardened some and humbled others. Which has it done to me?

entries.head: Alma 50:35

anchor.quote: he did cause that his men should march forth against them,

entries.reason: Teancum's earlier killing of Morianton in the field

targets.quote: Teancum did slay Morianton and defeat his army,
targets.verse_text: And it came to pass that the army which was sent by Moroni, which was led by a man whose name was Teancum, did meet the people of Morianton; and so stubborn were the people of Morianton, (being inspired by his wickedness and his flattering words) that a battle commenced between them, in the which Teancum did slay Morianton and defeat his army, and took them prisoners, and returned to the camp of Moroni. And thus ended the twenty and fourth year of the reign of the judges over the people of Nephi.
targets.markdown: And it came to pass that the army which was sent by Moroni, which was led by a man whose name was Teancum, did meet the people of Morianton; and so stubborn were the people of Morianton, (being inspired by his wickedness and his flattering words) that a battle commenced between them, in the which **Teancum did slay Morianton and defeat his army**, and took them prisoners, and returned to the camp of Moroni. And thus ended the twenty and fourth year of the reign of the judges over the people of Nephi.

targets.markdown: And it came to pass as he was about to do this, behold, **he was taken, and was tried according to the voice of the people, and condemned unto death**; for he had raised up in rebellion and sought to destroy the liberty of the people.
